decomposition.scheme: D(D) on N14 panda safety firmware (checker) + QM(D) on N11 openpilot driving software (doer)
decomposition.basis: ISO 26262-9 §5: an ASIL D requirement may be decomposed into D(D) and QM(D) when the elements are sufficiently independent.
decomposition.independence_argument_status: Open. Needs a dependent-failure analysis (ISO 26262-9 §7). Known common causes: the 12 V harness supply (its loss opens the relay and stops all output, which is the safe state) and the USB link (the panda checks every command it carries, and a silent link triggers the heartbeat timeout). The panda microcontroller gap (N13) must be closed before D(D) can be claimed for N14.

fsrs.fsr_text: The panda shall forward a steering command only while controls are allowed and only if it is within the brand safety mode's limits on magnitude, rate of rise and fall, deviation from the measured EPS torque or angle, and change per 250 ms; any other steering command shall be blocked and the limiter state reset.
fsrs.evidence: opendbc safety/lateral.h steer_torque_cmd_checks, steer_angle_cmd_checks; Toyota: XZACT equivalence 72/72 traces, 30/30 mutations

fsrs.fsr_text: The panda shall reject EPS torque and steering-angle messages whose checksum or quality flag is invalid, and end controls; it shall end controls if they are missing for more than 1 s (detected by the once-per-second check, so within 2 s).
fsrs.evidence: safety.h rx_msg_safety_check, safety_tick (1 s lag limit); Toyota quality flag on STEER_TORQUE_SENSOR

fsrs.fsr_text: The panda shall base speed-dependent steering limits on the slowest of the last six vehicle-speed samples and end controls on wheel-speed fault indications or missing wheel-speed messages.

The panda shall end controls when openpilot's heartbeat reports disengaged for 3 s while controls are allowed, and stop all output (SILENT, relay open) when the heartbeat is missing for 5 s with ignition on.
The panda shall detect a replaced stock command arriving from the vehicle (relay malfunction), latch the fault and block all output until the safety mode is set again.
The panda shall detect faults of its microcontroller (CPU, clock, RAM, flash) that could corrupt the safety firmware's decisions, and enter a no-output state with the relay open within the FTTI.
fsrs.evidence: Only a software watchdog on the main loop and interrupt-rate monitoring, which record faults; no lockstep core or independent hardware watchdog; reaction to a recorded fault not shown to be a no-output state

fsrs.fsr_text: The panda shall enforce a car safety mode only when it was selected for the recognized vehicle; a failed or unknown mode selection shall fall back to SILENT, and openpilot shall disengage if the panda's mode or parameter differs from the expected one.
fsrs.evidence: panda set_safety_mode fallback to SILENT; openpilot selfdrived controlsMismatch

fsrs.fsr_text: Only whitelisted steering message addresses, on the expected bus and with the expected length, shall be transmitted.
openpilot shall bound its own steering commands to the same limits the panda enforces, so that the checker is a backstop and not the primary limiter.
fsrs.evidence: opendbc car controllers apply CarControllerParams limits

fsrs.fsr_text: The panda shall forward a non-zero acceleration request only while controls are allowed and the gas pedal was not pressed in the previous frame, and only within the safety mode's range (Toyota: -3.5 to +2.0 m/s²); otherwise only the inactive value shall be sent.
The panda shall reject pedal and cruise-state messages that fail their checksum, and end controls if they are missing for more than 1 s (detected by the once-per-second check, so within 2 s).
fsrs.evidence: safety.h rx checks; Toyota PCM_CRUISE checksum

fsrs.fsr_text: Only whitelisted acceleration and cancel message addresses shall be transmitted; on vehicles in stock-longitudinal configuration only cancel requests are allowed.
fsrs.evidence: toyota.h ACC_CONTROL checks under stock longitudinal

fsrs.fsr_text: As FSR for SG-001 on the panda microcontroller.

The panda shall bound deceleration requests to the safety mode's minimum (Toyota: -3.5 m/s²) and allow non-zero requests only while controls are allowed. Unintended braking within that bound is a performance limitation analyzed under ISO 21448.
fsrs.evidence: longitudinal.h; intent is not checkable by the panda: see SOTIF (WP-CON-04)

fsrs.fsr_text: As FSR for SG-001 on the panda microcontroller.

The panda shall end controls on the rising edge of the brake, whenever the brake is pressed while moving, when stock cruise disengages, and when any checked vehicle message is invalid or late; without controls it shall block every actuating command.
Brake and cruise-state messages shall be checked for presence (missing for more than 1 s, detected within 2 s) and, where the vehicle provides it, checksum; their loss shall end controls.
fsrs.evidence: safety.h; Toyota BRAKE_MODULE (no checksum on the vehicle side: assumption ASM-V-03 must be verified)

fsrs.fsr_text: As FSR for SG-001 on the USB heartbeat.
As FSR for SG-001 on the panda microcontroller.
The panda shall allow controls only on the rising edge of the vehicle's stock cruise-engagement signal; openpilot shall have no means to grant controls.
fsrs.evidence: safety.h pcm_cruise_check; controls_allowed is only set inside the safety mode

fsrs.fsr_text: As FSR for SG-004 on the cruise-state message.
As FSR for SG-001 on the panda microcontroller.
openpilot shall issue an audible take-over request whenever lateral control is lost, saturated, or about to disengage, and shall not silently stop steering while engaged.
fsrs.status: Implemented upstream; timing to be specified
fsrs.evidence: openpilot selfdrived events (soft and immediate disable alerts)

fsrs.fsr_text: Take-over requests shall be both audible and visible, and shall remain active until the driver acknowledges or control is restored.
fsrs.status: Implemented upstream; verification to be specified

fsrs.fsr_text: openpilot shall issue an audible take-over request when the required deceleration exceeds what it may command, or when longitudinal control is lost.
fsrs.status: Implemented upstream; thresholds to be specified

fsrs.fsr_text: Driver monitoring shall escalate a visual alert, then an audible alert, then a disengagement with lockout when distraction lasts 5 s, 8 s and 13 s respectively, and shall fall back to the stricter 5/15/25 s wheel-touch policy when its estimate is uncertain for 10 s.
Loss or degradation of the driver-facing camera shall prevent engagement and disengage an active system with an alert.
fsrs.evidence: openpilot camera and driver-monitoring health events

fsrs.fsr_text: The displayed engagement state shall agree with the panda's controls-allowed state; openpilot shall disengage with an alert if the two disagree.
Engagement and disengagement shall each be signaled audibly as well as visually.
fsrs.status: Implemented upstream; verification to be specified

ftti_note: FTTIs are not set yet. They are to be derived per safety goal from vehicle-level tests (for example lateral deviation over time under the maximum allowed steering command), then checked against the mechanisms' reaction times: one CAN frame for limit checks and brake release, up to 2 s for message loss, 3 s and 5 s for heartbeat supervision.
